newsitem.title: USA: Case to buy British equipment manufacturer.
newsitem.headline: Case to buy British equipment manufacturer.

text.p: Case Corp said Monday it had agreed to purchase all outstanding shares of Fermec Holdings Ltd, a construction equipment manufacturer based in Britain.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed.
Fermec's 1995 revenues were about $155 million, up 70 percent since 1993, Case said.

"This is another strategic step we are taking to continue the profitable growth of our business," Jean-Pierre Rosso, Case chairman, said in a statement. "Fermec is an excellent fit with our global construction equipment business. It strengthens our product offering in the fast-growing light application sector and expands our market position in Europe and Asia."

Fermec's products include loader/backhoes, mini-excavators, skid steers and industrial tractors. The company employs about 580 people, most of whom are in Manchester, where the company has offices, a manufacturing plant and a parts depot. It also has a parts depot in France.
Fermec's products are sold in more than 90 markets worldwide.

"This acquisition underscores Case's commitment to the European construction equipment business," said Leopold Plattner, vice president and managing director, Case Europe. Case, with net sales of nearly $5.0 billion in 1995, said Fermec is the fourth acquisition it has made this year. Case makes and distributes agricultural and construction equipment.
